claims.claim_text: The authors present ReTrace, a method that turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step.
claims.excerpt: We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step.

claims.claim_text: The authors say LLM agents call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale; this is the problem ReTrace targets.
claims.excerpt: they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale.

claims.claim_text: ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step from the agent's reasoning, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it.
claims.excerpt: ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it.

claims.claim_text: The authors say only the final workflow-generation stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms.
claims.excerpt: Only this last stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms.

claims.claim_text: On 79 procedures from the authors' production platform, ReTrace workflows reach 93.8% completion versus 96.8% for the agent, at 24% lower cost per task.
claims.excerpt: On $79$ procedures from our production platform, ReTrace workflows reach $93.8\%$ completion, against $96.8\%$ for the agent, at $24\%$ lower cost per task.

claims.claim_text: On τ²-Bench, the authors report ReTrace workflows reach 75.8% task success versus 80.6% for the agent, and run in 1.3s instead of 170s.
claims.excerpt: they reach $75.8\%$ task success (agent: $80.6\%$) and run in $1.3$s instead of $170$s

claims.claim_text: The authors report that three rounds of repair on training failures lift k=2 workflows on τ²-Bench from 66.7% to 81.2%.
claims.excerpt: three rounds of repair on training failures lift $k{=}2$ workflows from $66.7\%$ to $81.2\%$.

claims.claim_text: On eight SOP-Bench procedures, the authors report ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation (80.6% vs. 83.6%).
claims.excerpt: On eight SOP-Bench procedures, ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation ($80.6\%$ vs. $83.6\%$)

claims.claim_text: The authors report that on SOP-Bench, repair from labeled training failures lifts ReTrace to 87.8% at 0.40s per task, compared to 85.5% in 46.6s for the agent.
claims.excerpt: but repair from labeled training failures lifts it to $87.8\%$ at $0.40$s per task, compared to $85.5\%$ in $46.6$s for the agent.
